h1: Car Window Tinting in Switzerland: Costs and Law
estratto: Costs, benefits and the Swiss rules (OETV) for tinting your car windows, explained in plain terms.

paragrafi: Tinting your car windows isn't just about looks: it improves privacy, protects against the sun and keeps the cabin cooler. In this guide we cover the real benefits, how much it costs in Switzerland and what the law allows, so you can choose without any surprises at inspection time.

sezioni.heading: The benefits of car window tinting
paragrafi: Tinting films offer real, practical benefits, not just a sharper look:
lista: Privacy and safety: less visibility from outside, and glass that holds the shards together if it breaks.
UV protection: they block up to 99% of ultraviolet rays, protecting your interior and your skin.
Less heat: the cabin stays cooler and you use the air conditioning less, saving on fuel.
Driving comfort: they cut glare and reflections, so your eyes tire less.

sezioni.heading: What Swiss law says
paragrafi: In Switzerland, window tinting is governed by the Ordinance on the Technical Requirements for Road Vehicles (OETV). The rules differ between the front and rear windows.
Front side windows and windscreen: they must let through at least 70% of light. Only clear anti-UV and heat-reducing films are allowed, ones that don't affect visibility.
Rear side windows and rear window: these can be tinted freely, with no limit on how dark they are. The only condition is that the car has external rear-view mirrors on both sides.

The sun strip at the top of the windscreen is permitted (Art. 71a OETV) as long as it doesn't reduce the driver's visibility. At inspection (MFK) the front windows are measured: non-compliant films must be removed, so always rely on approved materials.

sezioni.heading: How much car window tinting costs
paragrafi: The price doesn't depend on how dark the film is, but on the number of rear windows to be treated:
lista: 3 windows (two side windows plus the rear window): sedans and city cars
5 windows (four side windows plus the rear window): estate cars and many compacts

faq.domanda: Can you tint the front windows of your car in Switzerland?
faq.risposta: Only partly. The front windows and windscreen must let through at least 70% of light, so only clear anti-UV films are allowed. The rear side windows and rear window, on the other hand, can be tinted freely.

faq.domanda: How much does car window tinting cost?
faq.risposta: The cost depends on the number of rear windows (usually 3 to 9), not on how dark the film is. For an exact figure for your model, we'll prepare a free quote.

faq.domanda: Do tinted windows pass the vehicle inspection (MFK)?
faq.risposta: Yes, as long as the films comply with the regulations. At inspection the light transmission of the front windows is measured: with approved materials and professional installation there are no problems.

faq.domanda: How long does it take to install the films?
faq.risposta: Usually 3 to 5 hours, depending on the vehicle and the number of windows. After installation it's best to let the film cure for a few days before rolling the windows down.

faq.domanda: Do tinting films really protect against UV rays?
faq.risposta: Yes, quality films block up to 99% of UV rays. This protects your interior from fading and your passengers' skin on longer journeys.
